## 1. Cross-Cutting Seams
*Problems that emerge only where two domains compound. No single-domain reviewer owns them.*

### S1 — The "collect → display → never feed back" learning seam (Learning × Prompt × Onboarding) — **P1**
This is the single most repeated structural pattern in Argus, and it is invisible to domain audits because *each half is individually correct*:

| Signal collected (correct) | Displayed to user (correct) | Fed back into AI (MISSING) |
|---|---|---|
| Judgment override rates (`useJudgmentStore`) | "Your Judgment Patterns" card | `buildInitialAnalysisPrompt` ignores it (`user-context.ts:57-58` says so explicitly) |
| Persona accuracy ratings (`useAccuracyStore`) | Persona detail | `review-prompt.ts` never injects `worstAspects` |
| Reframe/rehearse evals (`eval-engine.ts`) | (local only) | Prompts are static; no mutation loop |
| `recallPastWork` precedent (`agent-tools.ts:46-90`) | (not surfaced) | Used silently or not at all |
| `learning-health.ts` assessment | (nowhere — test-only) | unused in app |

The moat tagline *"사용할수록 똑똑해집니다"* is contradicted at the integration layer. A correctness audit verifies the store writes; a UX audit verifies the card renders; **nobody owns the wire between them.** → **Track: Learning.** The cheapest high-leverage fix in the entire repo: pass `userContext` into `buildInitialAnalysisPrompt`/`buildDeepeningPrompt` (CLAUDE.md already documents how to inject pattern data safely as "참고:" reference-only).

### S2 — Silent data loss at scale (Data × Reliability × UX) — **P1**
`storage.ts:41-44` swallows `QuotaExceededError` into `console.error` with **zero UI feedback**. Compounded by: (a) progressive sessions grow unbounded (questions × answers × snapshots × 8 branches × N checkpoints, `useProgressiveStore`), and (b) timestamp merge (`db.ts` `mergeByTimestamp`) is clock-skew-vulnerable. A reliability audit sees "errors are caught." A UX audit sees "saves look successful." A data audit sees "caps exist (signals 500, evals 200)." None tests *week-50 heavy use*: the central session blob has no cap, hits quota, the write fails silently, the user reloads, work is gone. For a product whose entire premise is "don't lose your thinking," this is thesis-betraying. → **Track: Reliability + Data.** Make `setStorage` surface a toast on quota; add per-session byte budget + checkpoint pruning.

### S3 — Theater vs. reality at the trust-formation moment (Onboarding × Output × Prompt) — **P1**
The HeroFlow "team assembling" animation (`workspace/page.tsx:468-499`) stages 4 named persona avatars being "deployed," but `runInitialAnalysis` is a **single LLM call**. The "team" vanishes after the animation. This is the exact moment a skeptic decides "is this different from ChatGPT?" — and the honest answer in that moment is *no, it's one model with a costume*. An onboarding audit checks "does the animation play smoothly?" (yes). An output audit checks "is the snapshot good?" (yes). The **authenticity seam** — does the choreography reflect the execution model? — is unowned. → **Track: Onboarding.** Either make it real (per-persona observations) or drop the avatars for honest "Analyzing from multiple perspectives."

### S4 — The mobile bottom-bar collision (Reliability × UX × Design) — **P1**
Three independent fixed-position layers — `LogbookDrawer` (`bottom-[56px]`), `WorkerDrawer` (`bottom-0`), `QueryChatBar` — share no layout context and no deterministic z-order. With `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` on notched iPhones, they can co-occur and bury the **last 2-3 lines of ProgressiveFlow** — i.e., the final question or the "workers done" signal. Every component passes its isolated test (44px buttons, breakpoints exist); the *composition across a real voyage* was never tested. → **Track: UX (new sub-track: Mobile E2E).** Add a `useMobileBottomReserve()` hook that sums all fixed bottom elements + safe-area and applies one padding to the flow wrapper; fix z-order (Logbook 40 > Worker 41 > Chat 39).

### S5 — Synthesis manufactures false coherence (Prompt × Output × Reliability) — **P1**
`lead-agent.ts:142-200` instructs the lead to "make a judgment call" on contradicting workers — but nothing prevents it from *reframing genuine incompatibility as strategy* (Research: 40% demand; Finance: needs 60%; output: "lower-price repositioning opportunity" — coherent, signed by three experts, and wrong). Argus markets itself against the Siren's *fluent generic advice*; here it can produce a **better-written Siren song** that users trust *because* it's coherent. No domain audit asks "does synthesis hide contradictions?" → **Track: Output/Prompt.** Add a post-synthesis contradiction-detection pass that surfaces mutually-exclusive findings as explicit flags rather than narrative.

### S6 — Velocity outruns conviction (Prompt × UX × Onboarding) — **P2**
The progressive engine produces a full execution plan by round 3–5 in ~5 minutes; human direction-confidence doesn't grow that fast. Users feel swept into a detailed plan before they're sure of the *direction*, then get attached to it. A UX audit says "each step is clear"; the pacing-vs-certainty seam is orthogonal. → **Track: UX.** Add a round-3 "certainty checkpoint" that gates plan-deepening on user direction-confidence and decouples plan completeness from question count.

## 2. Product-Level Risks (Premortem Distilled)
*The riskiest unproven assumptions about whether anyone uses & returns. Flag as **NEW track: Product-validation** — none of these are "bugs," and a roadmap that only fixes domain findings could ship a polished product nobody returns to.*

### PV1 — Retention thesis is unvalidated; outputs are one-time markdown — **P0**
The 4 Ithaca outputs (Brief/Chain/Spec/Checklist) are static strings (`project-brief.ts`, `agent-spec.ts`). Strategic decisions are quarterly/annual, not daily — so a one-time-artifact tool has **no 7-day return reason**. The philosophy bets that *doing the thinking* is rewarding enough to return; users are outcome-seeking. **What would have to be true:** users return within 7 days for a *different* decision OR the artifacts become living (versioned checklist with persisted state, cross-project "last time the CEO doubted ROI" contextualization). Right now neither exists. → Validate: of users who generate outputs, what % use them in real work; what % run a 2nd voyage in 30 days. If <10%, the retention model is wrong, not the execution.

### PV2 — "Why not just ChatGPT?" has no answer *in the first run* — **P0**
Their own README names the real competitor as "just asking ChatGPT directly." But there's **zero forced friction** making structured thinking stick, and the value only reveals itself by the 3rd–4th refinement loop — past the churn cliff. The voyage metaphor is post-hoc justification for users who *already* believe thinking-before-acting matters (5–10% of TAM). **What would have to be true:** users who complete a full voyage report better outcomes than ChatGPT-direct >60% of the time. No A/B infra exists to know. → Add an active *judgment moment* in the first run ("Would ChatGPT have suggested something different? Does this reframe feel right?") so the differentiation is felt at minute one, not loop four.

### PV3 — The "5 promised moments" exist in the data, not in the user's awareness — **P1**
Reframe/clarity/discovery/convergence/meta-learning all occur structurally (`progressive-convergence.ts` computes the score; reframe diverges from surface task) but are **never signposted in the UI**. Convergence score is computed and nearly hidden. Meta-reflection (5th moment) is an optional checkbox with no surfaced payoff. Users leave with "a better document," not "I see my problem differently." The architectural sophistication domain audits validate is *invisible to users*. → **Track: UX/Onboarding.** Add moment-markers: divergence celebration, prominent convergence gauge (≥80% = ship-ready), mandatory 2-sentence reflection surfaced on revisit.

### PV4 — Solo-only data model caps TAM and kills word-of-mouth — **P2**
All stores are single-user; `Project` has no `team_members`, permissions, or shared decision log. Real strategic decisions are *organizational*. A consultant can't hand the live deliberation to a client team. → Don't build team mode yet — *validate first*: do >50% of completers share output and seek feedback? If yes, team mode is justified; if <10%, the solo thesis is right and team features would be cargo-cult.

### PV5 — The voyage metaphor has a half-life and doesn't compress — **P2**
Even the philosophy doc warns "비유를 학습해야 제품을 쓸 수 있다면 그 메타포는 실패한 것이다," yet button labels and headings often show *only* metaphor (`항로 재설정`) without the paired task name the doc itself mandates. Charming at run 1, friction at run 10, and impossible to explain in 30 seconds (word-of-mouth blocker). → A/B a metaphor-lite "classic mode"; enforce the doc's own "항해 어휘 + 업무명 병기" rule everywhere.

## 5. Prompt / Value Verdict — Does it beat "just ask ChatGPT"?

**Where it genuinely beats ChatGPT (real, defensible):**
- System prompts are *sharp*: they explicitly reject hedging ("그럴듯한 오답"), enforce authoritativeness, and bind reframing to execution. This is materially better than a cold ChatGPT prompt.
- The structured *sequence* (forced reframe → role split → rehearsal → refine) catches things a one-shot ChatGPT session won't, **for the user who completes it.**
- The logbook/voyage-trace concept is a real differentiator vs. a disposable chat thread — *if surfaced* (it currently isn't; it's a checkbox, ref the domain audit's Logbook findings).

**Where it does NOT beat ChatGPT (the honest gaps):**
1. **The Confidence Trap (P1).** The reframe self-rates `framing_confidence` 0–100 (`progressive-prompts.ts:45-49`) with **no post-hoc validation against the user's reality**. A brilliant, specific, uncomfortable reframe can pass every structural eval and still solve the *wrong* problem. The Siren isn't defeated — it's better-written. → Add a one-question reality checkpoint after reframe ("If you bet $10k this is right, what would you confirm first?").
2. **Evals measure structure, not truth (P1).** `REFRAME_EVALS` test `frame_shift`, `assumptions_non_generic`, `blind_spot_uncomfortable` — all structural. A clever redirect that's *disconnected from the real bottleneck* passes all of them. GIGO with better fonts.
3. **Rehearsal can become affirmation (P2).** Feedback intensity is user-selected; if set to soft, the pressure-test becomes a morale boost. No guarantee any persona ever *vetoes*. → Inject one background devil's-advocate persona that must surface ≥1 high-severity finding.
4. **First-run = ChatGPT-with-extra-words.** Type one sentence → 20–40s spinner → static markdown. The differentiating interactive Q&A loop starts at *interaction 2* — after the skeptic has already judged.

**Verdict:** The prompting is above-baseline and the structure adds real value *for completers*. But the value is **gated behind the first run and unvalidated against reality** — so for the skeptical first-timer it does not visibly beat ChatGPT, and even for completers there's no mechanism ensuring the confident-sounding output is *correct*.

*Invisible because:* the analytics layer is well-engineered and captures ~50 events; the gap is between "data exists" and "data answers 'are we winning?'" The team is flying blind on its own success criteria. *Do:* one SQL query per metric + daily threshold alerts (~4h).

Audit B said '7/9 metrics unmeasurable'; the real, scarier truth is the opposite — a SOPHISTICATED daily dashboard EXISTS (funnel, WoW, per-source completion, top-user) but some of its inputs are wired to dead event names, so the team is reading a dashboard that is confidently wrong in places. Only a production SQL query (SELECT distinct event_name FROM user_events) reconciled against the cron's expected names reveals this.

SILENT TELEMETRY BLACKOUT RISK. analytics.ts:168-179 does a fire-and-forget `supabase.from('user_events').insert()` with the ANON key, wrapped in try/catch that swallows everything, and `.then()` with no `.catch()`. If RLS on user_events ever denies anon INSERT (or the table is renamed/migrated), EVERY event silently drops and the daily report keeps emailing plausible-looking small numbers. There is no heartbeat/canary event and no dead-letter. A code audit sees 'errors handled'; a persona walkthrough never inspects the network tab. Only a live check (does a brand-new incognito session actually produce a row?) reveals whether telemetry is even flowing.

THE LLM COST/QUALITY BLIND SPOT. llm/route.ts:151 maps model 'strong' → Sonnet (with a comment 'using Opus here would raise costs') — so the product's most important reasoning step (synthesis, reframe) silently runs on the cheaper model regardless of what the UI implies. No per-call token/cost is logged to user_events (trackLLMCall records only duration_ms+success). So the team cannot answer 'what does one completed voyage cost us?' or 'did switching to Sonnet degrade reframe quality?' Neither a code audit nor a walkthrough surfaces unit economics — only a production cost/token telemetry query or an LLM eval harness against held-out reframes does.

RETENTION/OUTCOME GROUND TRUTH. Both audits assert the retention thesis is unvalidated (PV1), but neither can resolve it — it is empirically unknowable from code. The data to answer it is ALREADY being collected (progressive_sessions with phase, judgment_records, output_shared events) but no query computes 30-day re-voyage rate or output-used rate. This is a cohort-SQL question, not an audit question.

REAL-USER COMPREHENSION OF THE METAPHOR & THE FIRST 90 SECONDS. Whether a non-developer strategist understands '항로 재설정/리허설', feels the first static-markdown output beats ChatGPT, or rage-quits at the 20-40s spinner — none of this is in the code or inferable by a model role-playing a persona (the model already knows the product). Only a moderated 5-user test catches 'I didn't know what to type', 'I thought it froze', 'this is just a fancy ChatGPT'.

LOAD/CONCURRENCY BEHAVIOR OF THE JSONB SESSION MODEL. progressive_sessions stores the entire session as one JSONB blob; the atomic worker-update RPC does 6 nested jsonb_set calls per human reply. Under concurrent human-agent replies (Slack + email arriving together) plus the client's full-blob writes, last-writer-wins clobbering and RPC contention are plausible — but invisible to single-user code reading and single-user walkthroughs. Only a concurrency/load test surfaces it.

ABUSE & FINANCIAL SAFETY UNDER ADVERSARIAL TRAFFIC. Anon rate limiting hashes x-forwarded-for/x-real-ip (route.ts:104) — trivially spoofable/rotatable, and the server ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is the payer. A botnet or header-rotation could drain the owner's Anthropic budget. No spend cap, no alert. This is a production-traffic adversary scenario neither audit simulates.

CRON SINGLE-POINT-OF-FAILURE FOR ALL VISIBILITY. The ONLY production analytics surface is one daily email (vercel.json: one cron, 0 0 * * *) to REPORT_EMAIL via resend.dev's shared 'onboarding@resend.dev' from-address. If that email lands in spam, Resend's shared domain gets throttled, or the cron 500s (it returns 500 on send failure with only a console.error), the team goes blind with no in-app dashboard fallback. Invisible until the email simply stops arriving.
cheapest_highest_signal_probes: TELEMETRY RECONCILIATION (15 min, highest signal). Run in Supabase: `SELECT event_name, count(*) FROM user_events WHERE created_at > now()-interval '7 days' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;` Diff the result against every event name the daily-report cron expects (landing_hero_submit, flow_done, reframe_complete, recast_complete, progressive_draft_added/promoted, loop_converged, workspace_enter). Any expected name with 0 rows = a silently-broken dashboard metric. This alone will confirm the landing_hero_submit dead-event bug and any others.

TELEMETRY HEARTBEAT CANARY (30 min). Open the production site in a fresh incognito window, complete one reframe, then query `SELECT * FROM user_events WHERE session_id = '<the ov_sid from sessionStorage>'`. If rows are missing, telemetry is silently dropping (RLS/insert failure) and the entire daily report is fiction. Add a permanent `app_loaded` canary event + a daily alert if its count hits 0.

5-USER MODERATED FIRST-RUN TEST (half a day, the single highest product-signal probe). Recruit 5 non-developer strategists, give them one real decision, say nothing, screen-record. Measure: time-to-first-meaningful-input, did they understand the voyage metaphor unaided, did they call the first output 'better than ChatGPT' or 'the same', where they hesitated/quit. This de-risks PV1/PV2/PV3 and the metaphor half-life (PV5) in one session — none of which any audit can answer.

RETENTION/OUTCOME COHORT QUERY (1 hour). Two queries: (a) of users who hit phase='complete' in progressive_sessions, what % created a second session within 30 days; (b) of completed sessions, what % fired an output_shared or output_generated event afterward. <10% on either kills the static-artifact retention model empirically — turning audit B's PV1 hypothesis into a number.

LLM COST-PER-VOYAGE INSTRUMENTATION (2 hours). Add input/output token counts from the Anthropic response into the existing trackLLMCall payload, then query avg tokens per completed session × Sonnet pricing. Gives unit economics and lets you A/B reframe quality on Haiku vs Sonnet vs Opus with a small held-out eval set — answering 'is the cheap-model synthesis good enough' that route.ts:151 silently assumes.

ANON ABUSE / SPEND-CAP DRILL (1 hour). From a script, hammer /api/llm rotating x-forwarded-for headers; confirm whether you can exceed ANON_LIMIT and burn the server key. If yes, add a global daily Anthropic spend cap + an alert before any launch traffic. Cheap to test, existential if missed.

CONCURRENCY SMOKE TEST ON THE SESSION BLOB (2 hours). Script two simultaneous human-agent replies (or one Slack + one email) to the same progressive_session, plus a concurrent client full-blob save, and check for lost updates in the workers array. Validates the JSONB last-writer-wins risk that single-user testing structurally cannot.

CRON FAILURE ALARM (20 min). Make the daily-report return 200 with a logged warning on email failure instead of a silent 500, and add a second tiny cron (or Vercel monitor) that alerts if the report's own success ping is missing for a day — so 'we went analytics-blind' is itself an alerting event, not something noticed weeks later.
metaCritique.verdict: After both the domain audit (A) and the blind-spot sweep (B), the deepest still-invisible layer is the gap between what the code SAYS happens and what PRODUCTION actually does — a gap no static read or model-as-persona walkthrough can close. Audit B's headline 'instrumentation' finding is actually understated AND partly wrong in direction: a genuinely sophisticated daily-report cron already exists (funnel, WoW, per-source conversion, top-user), but (1) the user_events table has no migration in the repo at all — the analytics schema is unversioned and untestable, and (2) at least one funnel stage (landing_hero_submit) is wired to an event name emitted nowhere in app code (verified 0 emit-sites), so the team is reading a dashboard that is confidently wrong in places, with fire-and-forget inserts that could silently go to zero and nobody would know. That reframes the risk from 'no metrics' to 'trusted-but-unverified metrics,' which is more dangerous. The truly uncatchable classes are: telemetry integrity (needs a SQL reconciliation + a heartbeat canary), real-user comprehension of the metaphor and the first 90 seconds (needs a 5-user moderated test), unit economics and reframe quality across model tiers (route.ts:151 silently downgrades 'strong'→Sonnet; needs token telemetry + an eval set), retention as an empirical number (needs a cohort query against data already collected), and adversarial/load behavior (spoofable anon rate-limit on a server-paid API key; single-JSONB-blob concurrency). The cheapest decisive move is the 15-minute telemetry-reconciliation query — it costs almost nothing and immediately tells you whether the team's entire view of its own funnel is trustworthy. The single highest product-signal move is a half-day 5-user first-run test, which is the only instrument that can answer the existential PV1/PV2 questions that all the file:line analysis in the world cannot.
